skills.name: The modern kitchen: planning, management and shapes

worked_example.problem: In a kitchen the sink–cooker side is {a} m, cooker–fridge {b} m and fridge–sink {c} m. Is the work triangle well planned?
steps: Each side is between {sideMin()} m and {sideMax()} m, and the total is between {totalMin()} m and {totalMax()} m.

cards.idea: The work triangle joins the sink, the cooker and the fridge.
example: Short sides save steps; very short sides make the kitchen cramped.

cards.idea: Kitchen shapes: one-wall, galley, L-shaped, U-shaped, island.
Good management follows the order of work: store, prepare, cook, serve, wash.
example: Keep things near where they are used.

check.prompt: Put the order of work in a kitchen in order.

questions.prompt: The sides of a work triangle are {a} m, {b} m and {c} m. What is its total length?
The counters are shaded. Which kitchen shape is this?

misconceptions.explain: One wall: one-wall. Two facing rows: galley. Two walls at a corner: L. Three walls: U. A counter in the middle: island.

solution: Look at which walls have counters.

questions.prompt: Put the order of work in a kitchen in order.
A work triangle has sides {a} m, {b} m and {c} m. Is it well planned?
solution: Total = {triangleTotal(a, b, c)} m. Sides should be {sideMin()} m to {sideMax()} m and the total {totalMin()} m to {totalMax()} m.
